experiences.name: Mount Roberts Tram (Goldbelt Tram)
experiences.blurb: A six-minute ride from the cruise docks to about 1,800 feet with sweeping views and optional alpine walks. Low effort and right at the dock, IF it is running.
experiences.label: ideal_parents
experiences.mobility: Base station sits on the cruise docks (490 S. Franklin St). Wheelchair/ADA details are not on the operator's pages; call (907) 463-3412 before planning around it.
experiences.caveat: Do not plan around this attraction yet. See operating risk.

risk.text: The tram was closed all of the 2026 cruise season after an April crash. Goldbelt says it is confident it will be ready for 2027 but still needs a state certification evaluation and a replacement part (KTOO, Sep 24, 2026); the Juneau Independent (Jul 22, 2026) reported no date. As of 2026-11-07 no 2027 opening date was found. Treat as unavailable until the operator confirms.

experiences.name: Self-guided downtown Juneau walk (+ free Capitol tour)
experiences.blurb: Walk the compact downtown from the dock: a 12-stop self-guided loop of about 1.1 miles along South Franklin Street's boardwalks, plus the state Capitol's free weekday tour. No booking, no transport, leave whenever you like.
experiences.exertionBasis: planner judgment from the documented loop length
experiences.label: ideal_parents
experiences.mobility: Franklin Dock and the cruise terminal are fully wheelchair accessible with paved paths and ramps (CruiseHive). Downtown streets are narrow with wooden boardwalks; the city museum warns its own tours may include inclines, stairs and uneven ground.
experiences.caveat: Capitol tours run on weekdays only (1:30 and 3:00 pm in 2026; 2027 times not published) and can be cancelled. The AJ Dock berth is about a mile from town; a $5 shuttle runs (secondary source).
experiences.walkBasis: GPSmyCity's self-guided loop is about 1.1 mi starting at the cruise port; the Capitol tour is indoors.
experiences.stairsHills: Narrow streets and boardwalks; the museum notes possible inclines and stairs.

offers.provider: State Capitol (listed by the city museum)
offers.title: Alaska State Capitol tour
offers.note: Free, about 60 minutes, weekdays, no reservations (2026 schedule: 1:30 and 3:00 pm, last tour Sept 25). May be cancelled. 2027 schedule not published.

offers.title: Historic Downtown walking tour (guided)
offers.note: 2026 schedule: Tuesday to Thursday, 1:45 pm, last tour June 30 2026; 2027 dates not published, so it may not run when your ship is in. Reserve by phone. Accessibility not listed.

experiences.name: City bus to Mendenhall Glacier (do it yourself)
experiences.blurb: Capital Transit routes 3, 4 and 8 reach Dredge Lake Road, the stop nearest the visitor center, for a $2 adult fare. From there it is a flat, paved bike-path walk of about 1.5 miles each way. The cheapest way to the glacier, but the transit agency puts door to door at up to 1.5 hours each way.
experiences.exertionBasis: 3 miles of walking round trip before any visitor-center trails, plus long transit time
experiences.label: not_recommended
experiences.mobility: The walk from the stop is flat on a paved, wheelchair-accessible bike path (Capital Transit) but about 3 miles round trip, more than a 2-mile daily budget before reaching any trail.
experiences.caveat: Frequency is not stated on the transit page. Add the Forest Service visitor-center day fee ($5 now; see 'Mendenhall Glacier by bus'). Cash only, no change.
experiences.walkBasis: Dredge Lake Rd stop to the visitor center is about 1.5 mi each way (Capital Transit) = 3.0 mi, plus the 1/3 mi paved path (Forest Service map).
experiences.stairsHills: Flat paved path from the stop; the visitor center from the lots has stairs, elevators and an easy ramp.

offers.title: Adult fare, routes 3, 4 or 8 to Dredge Lake Road
offers.note: $2 cash for adults 19 and over, drivers cannot make change. The page does not say whether the fare is per boarding or whether a day pass exists: plan on $2 each way. Up to about 1.5 h each way including the walk.

experiences.name: Rent a car: Mendenhall Glacier at your own pace
experiences.blurb: Drive to Mendenhall Glacier Visitor Center (about 12 miles from downtown) and walk only as far as you like: the short paved path is about a third of a mile round trip, the gravel Nugget Falls trail about 2 miles round trip. No tour clock, but ship-day rental logistics and return hours matter.
experiences.exertionBasis: driving plus about a third of a mile on the paved path
experiences.label: ideal_parents
experiences.mobility: Visitor center: stairs, elevators and an easy ramp from the lots (Forest Service). A cruiser report says the Photo Point path is paved with an incline and the Nugget Falls trail is gravel and dirt and hard for wheelchairs.
experiences.caveat: No rental rate captured: no June 2027 price is published, and Juneau Car Rental's site blocks automated readers. A cruiser report (not first-party) says the downtown office is about a 20-minute walk from some berths and may close around 2 pm on cruise days; confirm drop-off hours and the cancellation terms. No source documents ship-day sell-outs; book early.
experiences.walkBasis: Paved 1/3 mi round trip plus lot and building walks (Forest Service map). The Nugget Falls gravel trail (2 mi round trip on the map; 0.8 mi on the trail page, direction not stated) is optional and would break a 2-mile budget.
experiences.stairsHills: Stairs/elevators/ramp at the visitor center; Photo Point path inclined; Nugget Falls gravel, gentle slope.

offers.provider: Rental cars near the Juneau docks (Juneau Car Rental, Avis; cruiser-reported)
offers.title: One-day rental car for Mendenhall
offers.note: No published June 2027 daily rate captured. Airport rentals are generally cheaper but need a cab or timed bus (forum). Add the $5 Forest Service day fee.

experiences.name: Hike from downtown: Perseverance or Mount Roberts Trail
experiences.blurb: Free trails start at Basin Road, about a mile from the docks. Perseverance Trail is rated moderate at about 3 miles along a former rail line; the Mount Roberts Trail is rated difficult and steep. Rain gear and a firm return-to-ship time are essential.
experiences.exertionBasis: alaska.org difficulty ratings plus about 2 mi round trip to the trailhead
experiences.label: brothers
experiences.mobility: Steep, uneven mountain trails: not suitable for the parents.
experiences.caveat: alaska.org does not say whether Perseverance's 3 miles is one way or round trip, and it gives no length or gain for Mount Roberts. Check the trail distances with the Forest Service before relying on the time.
experiences.walkBasis: About 1 mi each way to the Basin Road trailhead (alaska.org) plus Perseverance Trail at about 3 mi; 5 mi is the minimum, up to about 8 mi if the 3 mi is one way.
experiences.stairsHills: Steep climbing on Mount Roberts; Perseverance climbs gradually above Gold Creek.

offers.title: Perseverance Trail or Mount Roberts Trail
offers.note: No fee found on the alaska.org pages. Trail conditions and any bear or weather closures are not captured.

experiences.name: SMART bus and shuttle (skip the dock-to-town walk)
experiences.blurb: The SMART bus runs from the cruise dock to downtown from 7 am to 9 pm when ships are in: $3 each way or $5 all day. An on-demand shuttle also reaches the Skagway River Bridge ($5), the end of pavement on Dyea or Liarsville Road ($10) and Dyea ($15). It saves most of the roughly mile-long walk to Broadway.
experiences.exertionBasis: planner judgment: removes about 1.8 miles of walking for the parents
experiences.label: ideal_parents
experiences.mobility: CruiseHive says every terminal and pier is wheelchair accessible and that shuttles help guests with mobility needs; the vehicles' own accessibility features were not found.
experiences.caveat: The on-demand shuttle needs 24 hours' notice outside regular hours and its fares are per person. Check the bus runs when your ship is in; the page says 'when cruise ships are in port'.
experiences.walkBasis: With the bus, only the dock-side stop to your destination and about 0.5 mi along Broadway remain (versus about 2.3 mi walking from the dock).
experiences.stairsHills: Flat town; vehicle steps.

offers.title: SMART bus: all-day pass, dock to downtown
offers.note: Pay the driver; 7 am to 9 pm daily when cruise ships are in port.

offers.title: SMART bus: one way, dock to downtown
offers.note: Pay the driver. Cheaper than the day pass only for a single leg.

offers.title: On-demand shuttle: dock to Dyea
offers.note: Per person. Book ahead, 24 hours' notice outside regular hours. Cheaper zone stops: River Bridge $5, end of pavement on Dyea or Liarsville Road $10. Dyea road is gravel past the end of pavement.

experiences.name: Yakutania Point walk (self-guided)
experiences.blurb: A short, easy NPS-listed walk from town: 1 to 2 miles round trip with about 100 feet of climb, a footbridge and rock steps. Free, and the nearest of Skagway's trails to the docks, but the dock walk adds to the total.
experiences.exertionBasis: NPS rates it easy; rock steps and outcrops plus the dock-to-town walk
experiences.label: precautions
experiences.mobility: NPS describes a trail through alders with a footbridge, rock steps and rock outcroppings; surface and wheelchair access are not stated. Plus the dock-to-town walk unless you take the SMART bus.
experiences.caveat: NPS gives distances from its visitor center (2nd Ave and Broadway), not from the docks.
experiences.walkBasis: Up to 2 mi round trip on the trail (NPS) plus about 1.8 mi round trip between the dock and the NPS visitor center (CruiseHive: under a mile each way). With the SMART bus: about 2.4 mi.
experiences.stairsHills: Rock steps and a footbridge; about 100 ft of gain.

offers.title: Yakutania Point trail
offers.note: Free public trail; distances round trip from the NPS visitor center.

experiences.name: Gold Rush Cemetery and Lower Reid Falls (self-guided)
experiences.blurb: NPS lists it as easy: about 4 miles round trip with 50 feet of climb, on a gravel road and then a short forest trail, starting north of downtown behind the railroad yards. Free. With the dock walk it is a long outing for most travelers.
experiences.exertionBasis: NPS easy rating, but about 6 miles of walking in total with the dock walk
experiences.label: brothers
experiences.mobility: Gravel road then a short forest trail; wheelchair access not stated. Far beyond a 2-mile daily budget for the parents.
experiences.caveat: Directions in the NPS listing cross the highway and pass behind the railroad yards; confirm the route is open and safe on your day.
experiences.walkBasis: 4 mi round trip from the NPS visitor center (NPS) plus about 1.8 mi round trip from the dock (CruiseHive: under a mile each way).
experiences.stairsHills: Flat-ish; about 50 ft of gain.

offers.title: Gold Rush Cemetery and Lower Reid Falls
offers.note: Free public trail; distances round trip from the NPS visitor center.

experiences.name: Lower Dewey Lake hike (self-guided)
experiences.blurb: The classic steep climb above town: 0.9 miles to the lake or 3.6 miles around it, about 500 feet of gain, with a wooden staircase and rocky sections. Free. For the brothers; allow a firm turn-around time.
experiences.exertionBasis: NPS moderate rating with 500 ft of climb and steep uphill sections
experiences.label: brothers
experiences.mobility: Wooden staircase, footbridge, steep uphill, earthen levee and rocky sections (NPS): not suitable for the parents.
experiences.caveat: Trailhead is east on 2nd Ave past the depot, then north along the tracks (NPS).
experiences.walkBasis: 3.6 mi around the lake (NPS) plus about 1.8 mi round trip from the dock; the 0.9 mi out-and-back to the lake alone would total about 3.6 mi.
experiences.stairsHills: About 500 ft of climb on stairs and steep trail.

offers.title: Lower Dewey Lake trail
offers.note: Free public trail; distances from the NPS visitor center.

experiences.name: Rent a car: Klondike Highway toward Carcross and Emerald Lake
experiences.blurb: A rental car lets you drive the scenic highway north from Skagway at your own pace. Passports are required if you cross into Canada. Rental desks are in town; whether each company allows the Canada drive was not found in writing, so ask before you book.
experiences.label: ideal_parents
experiences.mobility: Seated in the car; stops are roadside. No wheelchair statement applies; vehicle choice is yours.
experiences.caveat: No renter's written Canada policy was found: Cruise Critic posters say US citizens can take a US rental into Canada with passports and that Avis cars are barred from gravel roads such as Dyea Road. Border hours and drive times were not captured; the US inspection station is on the highway (Mile 6.8). Counter lines were reported on ship days; no sell-out data. Confirm return hours against your all-aboard time.
experiences.walkBasis: Car-based; short roadside stops and rental-desk walks. Affordable Car Rentals is at 648 Broadway, about the end of the compact downtown.
experiences.stairsHills: None on foot beyond stops.

offers.provider: Affordable Car Rentals; Drive About Car Rental (listed by Skagway visitor bureau)
offers.title: One-day rental car, Klondike Highway
offers.note: No published June 2027 daily rate captured; an aggregator's Turo-branded November price is not comparable. Sourdough and Avis are also mentioned by cruisers; Avis's Skagway page did not load.

experiences.name: Self-guided: Creek Street, Totem Heritage Center and waterfront
experiences.blurb: Ketchikan's compact waterfront is walkable from the downtown berths: Creek Street's boardwalk (allow 1 to 2 hours with Dolly's House) and the Totem Heritage Center about a 15-minute walk from downtown. Princess also sells a gentle 9-block walking tour that is listed wheelchair accessible.
experiences.exertionBasis: flat boardwalks and short walks; some hills and stairs downtown
experiences.label: ideal_parents
experiences.mobility: Princess lists its walking tour Easy and wheelchair accessible (electric chairs and scooters accommodated; manual chairs need to complete the tour alone or with a companion). Creek Street's boardwalk is flat but slippery when wet.
experiences.caveat: Applies to downtown berths only; Ward Cove calls need a shuttle first. Totem Heritage Center admission and hours were not captured. Distances are not measured on any page.
experiences.walkBasis: Princess walking tour is about 9 blocks; Totem Heritage Center is about a 15-minute walk from downtown (about 0.7 mi each way) = 1.5 mi round trip, plus Creek Street.
experiences.stairsHills: Some downtown hills and stairs (secondary source); Creek Street boardwalk flat.

offers.title: Creek Street and downtown waterfront on foot
offers.note: No admission found to walk Creek Street or the waterfront; not separately sourced.

offers.title: Historical Ketchikan and Creek Street Walking Tour
offers.note: About 9 blocks. The page shows no price. Guests with disabilities must contact the onboard tour office at least 48 hours ahead.

offers.title: Totem Heritage Center admission
offers.note: Admission and hours were not captured.

experiences.name: City bus to Totem Bight State Park (do it yourself)
experiences.blurb: The borough bus north from the docks enters Totem Bight State Historical Park in about 25 minutes. It runs roughly hourly, so the return needs planning. From Ward Cove the same bus is about 5 minutes and 3 miles away, which makes it a cheap alternative to the Ward Cove shuttle.
experiences.exertionBasis: short stop walks plus the park trail; hourly bus adds timing risk
experiences.label: precautions
experiences.mobility: The whole bus fleet is wheelchair accessible (alaska.org). At Totem Bight the bus stops inside the park, a short walk from the trail start and self-pay station; park surfaces were not captured.
experiences.caveat: Schedule and fare come from a May 2023 blog; alaska.org lists an older $1 fare; the borough's fares and schedule pages were not read. Confirm the summer 2027 timetable and last bus before relying on it. Park entry is paid by card at a self-pay station.
experiences.walkBasis: Stop in front of a coffee shop near the port (5 to 10 minutes from the farthest berth) plus a short walk in the park; park trail length not captured.
experiences.stairsHills: Not captured; the bus entrance is inside the park.

offers.title: Bus to Totem Bight (cash fare per ride)
offers.note: $2 cash per ride per a May 2023 blog; about hourly (northbound near :25, return near :13 in that timetable); about 25 minutes from the port. alaska.org lists $1. Bring dollar bills, no change.

offers.title: Totem Bight State Historical Park entry
offers.note: $5 per a May 2023 blog, paid by card at a self-pay station. Not read on the state's own page.

experiences.name: Rent a car: Totem Bight, Settlers Cove and the Ward Lake loop
experiences.blurb: Drive north to Totem Bight State Park, Settlers Cove and Ward Lake at your own pace. A cruiser reports Settlers Cove about a 20-minute drive from town, Totem Bight about 10 minutes beyond it, and the Ward Lake nature loop at 1.3 miles and flat. Easy on the legs, but rental logistics matter.
experiences.exertionBasis: driving plus a flat 1.3-mile loop (cruiser report)
experiences.label: ideal_parents
experiences.mobility: Settlers Cove has gentle slopes and a few sets of stairs; Ward Lake's 1.3-mile loop is flat (cruiser report). No first-party accessibility information.
experiences.caveat: No rental rate captured; one cruiser's roughly $60 for the day is an anecdote and is not stored as a price. The same poster says Alaska Car Rental picked up and returned at the dock; confirm that and the return hours. No source documents ship-day sell-outs; book early.
experiences.walkBasis: Ward Lake loop 1.3 mi (cruiser report) plus parking-lot walks; skip the loop for a shorter day.
experiences.stairsHills: A few stair sets at Settlers Cove; Ward Lake loop flat.

offers.title: One-day rental car
offers.note: No published June 2027 rate captured. A forum anecdote of about $60 for a day is not used as a price.

experiences.name: Deer Mountain Trail (self-guided hike)
experiences.blurb: Ketchikan's classic climb starts near downtown: 5 miles with about 2,600 feet of gain, rated difficult. Free, but it is a long, steep day for the brothers and needs a firm turn-around time in a wet climate.
experiences.exertionBasis: alaska.org: difficult, 5 miles, about 2,600 ft gain
experiences.label: brothers
experiences.mobility: Steep mountain trail: not suitable for the parents.
experiences.caveat: alaska.org does not say whether 5 miles is one way or round trip; assume round trip unless the Forest Service says otherwise. The trailhead is a gravel lot just up Ketchikan Lakes Road, roughly half a mile from downtown by its directions.
experiences.walkBasis: 5 mi trail (alaska.org) plus roughly 1 mi each way between the berths and the trailhead (planner estimate); higher if 5 mi is one way.
experiences.stairsHills: About 2,600 ft of steep climbing.

offers.title: Deer Mountain Trail
offers.note: No fee found on the alaska.org page.

phase3.summary: Juneau, Skagway and Ketchikan: walkMiles, walkConfidence, walkBasis and stairsHills on every existing experience; 13 new DIY or budget experiences (rental car, public bus or shuttle, self-guided walks, free hikes). walkMiles is a conservative one-person planning figure (dock to start, on-tour walking, back to the dock; higher end of any range). walkConfidence: documented (a published length), derived (arithmetic from published lengths) or estimate (planner judgment; no operator figure).
